title: She Was Trained to Kill by Her Own Father — and on Thursday, Alia Bhatt Rewrites the YRF Spy Universe
excerpt: Alpha drops July 3 with 75 million teaser views, a Hrithik Roshan cameo, and the franchise's first female-led origin story — here's why it's the most dangerous Bollywood release of the summer
body:
The countdown on **Alia Bhatt**'s Instagram has been ruthless. Seven days. Six. Five. Each post darker than the last — smudged kohl, split knuckles, a stare that could stop a bullet mid-flight. No smiles. No soft focus. No florals. This is not the Alia you know from *Rocky Aur Rani* or *Gangubai*. This is someone who has been broken down and rebuilt, and the first time you see her in the **Alpha** teaser, hand-to-hand combat in what looks like a rain-soaked Eastern European alley, you understand immediately: she didn't come here to charm anyone.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0</youtube>

The teaser dropped on June 10 and clocked **75 million views in 24 hours** — the kind of number that makes studio executives rethink their entire year. **SS Rajamouli**, **Shah Rukh Khan**, **Priyanka Chopra**, and **Salman Khan** all publicly praised it within a day, which in Bollywood terms is the equivalent of a standing ovation at Cannes. But the real story isn't the numbers. It's what Yash Raj Films has done with the franchise.

## The Origin Story Nobody Expected

For years, the **YRF Spy Universe** has been a boys' club. **Tiger** (Salman Khan) kicked doors down. **Kabir** (Hrithik Roshan) looked gorgeous doing it. **Pathaan** (Shah Rukh Khan) made it personal. Each film was louder, glossier, more expensive than the last — ₹300 crore budgets, global shoots, enough testosterone to power a small nation.

Alpha changes the architecture. Directed by **Shiv Rawail** (who proved his nerve with *The Railway Men*), the film tells the origin story of a girl moulded into India's deadliest operative — by her own father. **Bobby Deol** plays that father, and the trailer makes it devastatingly clear that his love and his training are the same thing. He doesn't protect her from danger. He *is* the danger.

**Sharvari Wagh** stands beside Alia with equal ferocity, their chemistry crackling with the tension of two women who were built to be weapons and are only now deciding who they want to point at. **Anil Kapoor** rounds out the cast as R&AW chief Colonel Vikrant Kaul — because every spy universe needs a man in a suit who knows too much.

And then there's the moment the trailer saved for last: a blink-and-you-miss-it glimpse of **Hrithik Roshan** reprising Major Kabir Dhaliwal from *War*. Social media didn't miss it. The internet combusted.

## What the Trailer Tells Us

The full trailer, released June 17, is a different beast from the teaser. Where the teaser was mood — rain, fists, silence — the trailer is spectacle. Large-scale explosions across what appears to be three continents. A chase sequence through a Middle Eastern bazaar that plays like a Bourne film directed by someone who grew up on Rohit Shetty. Hand-to-hand combat choreography that's clearly influenced by *The Raid* more than any previous YRF entry.

But the emotional hook is the betrayal at the centre of the story. Bobby Deol's character doesn't just train Alpha — he trained her to be used *against* India. The film appears to follow Alia and Sharvari as they untangle their own programming and choose their own side. It's a spy film, yes, but it's also a story about daughters and the men who shaped them.

> "Alpha is more than a character or a film title — it's an attitude."
> — Yash Raj Films

## The Numbers Game

Alpha arrives on **July 3** after being preponed from July 10 — a strategic move by producer **Aditya Chopra** to grab two clean weeks before *Dhamaal 4* and Christopher Nolan's *The Odyssey* crowd the multiplex. It shares its opening day only with Huma Qureshi's *Baby Do Die Do*, which shouldn't dent its screen count.

The YRF Spy Universe has a combined worldwide gross exceeding ₹3,000 crore across *Ek Tha Tiger*, *Tiger Zinda Hai*, *War*, *Pathaan*, and *Tiger 3*. If Alpha can match even *Tiger 3*'s ₹466 crore worldwide, it'll be Alia Bhatt's biggest commercial hit since *Gangubai Kathiawadi* — and it'll prove that the franchise doesn't need a Khan to print money.

## Where to Watch

Alpha releases in cinemas worldwide on **July 3, 2026**, in **Hindi** with shows across **IMAX** and premium formats. For the diaspora in the US, UK, and Canada, advance bookings are expected to open by June 30 through Fandango, Cineplex, and local chains. No OTT date has been announced — YRF typically holds theatrical windows for 6-8 weeks before streaming.

This is the film Alia Bhatt has been building toward for a decade. Every delicate performance, every awards-season darling turn — it was all prologue. On Thursday, she picks up a gun, and she doesn't look like she plans to put it down.
